title: Accelerated patch lanes and cherry-pick governance for LTS and semver maintenance
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define and implement an operational model for fast, auditable patch delivery across semantic-versioned channels and the LTS stream. This ticket scopes a dual-lane approach: an emergency lane for severity-critical fixes with shortened gates and an LTS maintenance lane for scheduled backports. Includes branch naming conventions, automated cherry-pick tooling, ownership rules, and integration with rollout gates and monitoring dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: A clear severity-to-lane mapping published and shared with oncall and release owners
Branch naming and tagging conventions documented and enforced by CI checks
Auto-cherry-pick bot prototype opens PRs to target maintenance branches and adds a clear audit trail
Rollout gate configuration (canary percentages, health checks) applied automatically for emergency-lane releases
Backports include automated test selection run in a representative LTS staging environment
Runbook updated with explicit escalation paths and post-deploy verification checklist
steps: Draft severity matrix aligning customer-visible impact, internal SLO breach risk, and allowed lanes
Define branch topology: release/main, stable-X.Y (LTS), maintenance/X.Y.Z and emergency/x.y.z-quick
Implement CI gating rules: block merges to stable branches without signed-off cherry-pick PRs
Build an "auto-cherry" GitHub Action to create backport PRs, add reviewers, and tag PRs with source commit and incident id
Wire rollout gates: integrate Console rollout policies so emergency-lane releases default to 5% canary with automatic rollback on key metric regressions
Create test matrix for backports: smoke + selective integration tests that cover KV cache, batching, and auth flows
Add dashboards and alerts: per-lane health panels and a post-release checklist webhook that pings the release channel
Run a simulated emergency exercise and a scheduled LTS backport dry-run and document findings
